Gold Catalysis Enabling Furan-Fused Cyclobutenes as a Platform
toward Cross Cycloadditions
Shouzhi Zhang, § Aijie Tang, § Ruyu Xie, Zhiqiang Zhao, Jinzhong Yao, and Maozhong Miao *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3701 −3705 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: The inherently strained furan-fused cyclobutenes, in situ generated via
cycloisomerizations of allenyl ketones bearing cyclopropyl moiety under gold catalysis,
have been utilized as reactive building blocks toward cross cycloadditions. The [4 + 2] and
[3 + 2] annulations of these species with benzo[ c]isoxazoles and N-iminoquinazolinium
ylides furnish various three-dimensional cyclobutane-bridged polyheterocycles in good
yields. A wide range of typically electron-de ﬁcient 1,3-dienes, heterodienes, and 1,3-dipoles
can trap furan-fused cyclobutenes to a ﬀord several polycyclic architectures.
P
olyheterocycles with a cyclobutane functionality at the
fused junction are important structural motif in many
natural products1 (I, II, III) and also behave as a new glycoluril
diether, one kind of supramolecular precursors 2 (IV) with a
wide dihedral angle on the concave face ( Scheme 1 A).
Classical procedures, such as [2 π+2π]-photocycloaddition,3
ring-expansion of cyclopropane, 4 nucleophilic ring-closure, 5
transition-metal catalyzed cyclization, 6 and so on, have been
developed for the construction of cyclobutane-containing
architecturally complex molecules. However, these methods
have often su ﬀered from inconvenient reaction conditions, low
selectivities, and inaccessibility of substrates. Hence, the
development of a general, diversity-oriented and stereo-
selective strategy to access polyheterocycles with a highly
strained cyclobutane at the bridged-carbons poses signi ﬁcant
challenges and is highly desirable.
The cross cycloaddition of highly reactive organo-
intermediates has emerged as a hot topic in chemistry for
two decades and has been regarded as a reliable tool for rapidly
constructing complex sca ﬀolds.
7 Cyclobutenones8 and their
heterocyclic analogues 9 are among highly useful building
blocks toward some cycloadditions for the construction of
molecules with four-membered rings remained at the joint
position ( Scheme 1 B). Generally, the inner C −C double in
these substrates shows dramatically enhanced reactivities
because of the higher strained energy of small ring systems
(ca. 26.7 kcal mol
−1) relative to normal cycles. In 2010,
Danishefsky10 reported an elegant work on Diels −Alder
cycloaddition employing the parent cyclobutenone as reactive
dienophile to react with simple dienes and Danishefsky ’s
dienes to a ﬀord bicycle[4.2.0]octenes with excellent selectivity
(Scheme 1 B, eq 1). Recently, Lu 11 disclosed an asymmetric
version of Diels −Alder reaction using 3-methoxycarbonylcy-
clobutenone as the dienophile. Besides, Didier 12 presented the
novel dipolar cycloadditions for the stereoselective formation
of fused isoxazoline derivatives involving azetines and thietes,
the heterocyclic analogs of cyclobutenes ( Scheme 1 B, eq 2).
To our best knowledge, electron-rich cyclobutenes as
dienophiles for the Diels −Alder reaction or as highly active
species for dipolar cycloadditions are however still under-
developed. Furthermore, homogeneous gold catalysis
13 has
empowered a wide array of e ﬃcient transformations to enter
structurally complex molecules based on the unique ability of
gold complexes to interact with π-bonds. In this area, we
14
have developed a gold-catalyzed tandem cycloisomerization of
cyclopropyl-tethered allenyl ketones to produce the key
intermediates, furan-fused cyclobutenes, which could be
further transformed into gold-containing 1,4-all-carbon dipoles
for [4 + n] cycloadditions to produce various furan-based
polycyclic molecules ( Scheme 1 C). We envisioned that the in
situ formed furan-fused cyclobutenes with highly strained
electron-donating double bond might display novel reactivities
toward cycloadditions. Herein, we would like to disclose the
new gold-catalyzed reactions of allenyl ketones bearing a
cyclopropyl moiety, which enable the in situ furan-fused
cyclobutenes as platform for [2 + n] cycloadditions for the

(Scheme 1 C).
To fulﬁll our hypothesis, we initially treated the cyclopropyl-
tethered allenyl ketone ( 1a) with benzo[ c]isoxazole ( 2a) with
10 mol % of PPh 3AuOTf in DCE at room temperature (rt)
under N 2 atmosphere for 12 h. The [4 + 2] cycloadduct 4a
bearing a strained cyclobutane and O-bridged ring was
obtained in 36% yield with excellent stereoselectivity ( Scheme
2). The reaction parameters i ncluding metal catalysts,
additives, ligands, temperature, and solvents were systemati-
cally varied (see Table S1 in the Supporting Information (SI)
for details). Other metal catalysts such as Pd(OAc) 2, CuI, and
Cu(OTf)2 were incapable of catalyzing this transformation
(Table S1 , entries 2 −4). The examination of counteranion
eﬀects15 indicated that the SbF 6 anion gave the best results,
because counterions like SbF 6
− have smaller a ﬃnity toward
cationic gold, which may show higher reactivity in this
transformation (Table S1, entries 5 −8). Reducing the amount
of PPh
3AuCl did not result in inferior yields ( Table S1 , entry
9), while the use of an increasing amount of AgSbF 6 up to 15
mol % led to higher yields ( Table S1, entry 10). Ligand e ﬀects
of gold catalysts indicated that the employment of more
crowded t-BuXPhosAuCl would greatly improve the yield of 4a
up to 72% ( Table S1 , entries 11 −16). No better yields of
product 3a were gained by reducing or elevating the reaction
temperature ( Table S1 , entries 18 and 19). DCE is the best
choice of solvent because the reaction performed in other
solvents such as DCM, chloroform, THF, toluene, acetonitrile,
and DMF all gave decreased yields ( Table S1, entries 20 −25).
Lastly, we checked the reaction using 5 mol % of AgSbF
6 as
sole catalyst in DCM; indeed, the target 4a could be obtained,
albeit in modest yield (55%). Thus, the standard conditions
were established as cyclopropyl-tethered allenyl ketone 1a (1
equiv) and benzo[ c]isoxazole 2a (3 equiv) using t-
BuXPhosAuCl (2 mol %)/AgSbF
6 (15 mol %) as a catalytic
system in a solution of DCE (0.1 M) at rt ( Scheme 2 ).
With the standard conditions in hand, the scope of gold-
catalyzed [4 + 2] cycloaddition was investigated, and the
results were summarized in Scheme 3 . First, a wide range of
benzo[c]isoxazoles 2 were employed to react with cyclopropyl
tethered allene ketone 1a. Benzo[c]isoxazoles bearing Cl, Br,
NO
2, and CO 2Me groups at the C6 position of the aromatic
ring reacted smoothly with 1a to deliver the corresponding
4b−4e in moderate to high yields. Meanwhile, the halo
substituents could be suitably arranged in the C5 position of
benzo[c]isoxazole frameworks to a ﬀord products 4f−4h in
moderate yields. Subsequently, the substrate scope of cyclo-
propyl tethered allene ketones 1 was then evaluated. The
nature of the substituents attaching at the benzene ring of R
1
position had little e ﬀect on this reaction, and the desired
compounds 4i−4p were produced in 54 −78% yields. 2-
Naphthyl, 2-thienyl, and 2-furyl groups were also well tolerated
at the R
1 position, furnishing the desired products ( 4q−4s)i n

aromatic rings were all compatible for this transformation, and
the cycloadducts 4t−4z were obtained in modest to high
yields. To our delight, a cycloheptyl fused substrate could be
successfully used for the assembly of the highly bridged-
skeleton 4aa in 50% yield.
Encouraged by the aforementioned results of Diels −Alder
cycloaddition involving the in situ formed furan-fused cyclo-
butenes as an ideal dienophile, we wondered whether the
furan-fused cyclobutenes could be subjected to the dipolar
cycloadditions. Thus, we explored the [3 + 2] cycloaddition
using cyclopropyl-tethered allenyl ketone ( 1a) and quinazolin-
3-ium-3-yl(tosyl)amide ( 2a) as model substrates under gold
catalysis. The structurally complex cycloadduct 5a was
furnished in 40% yield with 8:1 diastereoselectivity at the
initial attempt. Systematic screenings of the conditions were
then carried out (see Table S2 in the Supporting Information
(SI) for details). The yield of 5a was greatly improved when
the reaction was carried out using Ph
3PAuCl (1 mol
%)/AgSbF6 (10 mol %) as the catalytic system in a solution
of EA (0.1 M) at rt ( Scheme 4 ).
The scope of this novel [3 + 2] cycloaddition reaction was
shown in Scheme 5 . A variety of N-iminoquinazolinium ylides
3 bearing electron-withdrawing or electron-donating groups at
the aromatic ring of the quinazoline backbone were well-
tolerated to provide 5b−5h in modest to good yields. Various
substituted sulfonyl functionalities were compatible, giving 5i−
5m in high yields. With respect to cyclopropyl-tethered allene
ketones 1,d iﬀerent aromatic substituents ( 5n−5u), alkyl ( 5v),
and heterocyclic substituents ( 5w−5x) were suitably arranged
at the R
1 position, leading to high yields of products. Varying
the substituents at the R 2 position gave the cycloadducts 5y−
5ad in high to good yields. The cycloheptyl or cyclooctyl-fused
cyclopropyl-tethered allene ketones were also suitable
substrates to a ﬀord 5ae and 5af in 71% and 40% yield,
respectively.
To demonstrate the synthetic utilities of these cyclo-
additions, the transformations of the products were performed
(Scheme 6 ). The reductive cleaving of the N −O bond of 4a
furnished quinoline derivative 6 in 89% yield. Compound 6
could be further transformed into 7a and 7b via selective N-
alkylation and oxidation in high yields. Moreover, the ring-
expansion reaction of 5a in the presence of TfOH (2 equiv)
aﬀorded the seven-membered ring fused heterocycle 8 in a
high yield, which could be further reduced to produce 9 under
Raney Ni/H
2 system in an acceptable yield.
Finally, it is worth noting that the in situ formed furan-fused
cyclobutenes could be captured by a wide range of other π-
components including di ﬀerent 1,3-dienes, heterodienes, and
1,3-dipoles. Some representative examples are showed in
Scheme 7 . For instance, the highly reactive 1,3-diphenyliso-
benzofuran 10 was compatible to this cycloaddition to give
highly bridged heterocycle 11 in 62% yield with well-de ﬁned
stereoselectivity. The reactions of the electron-de ﬁcient 1,3-
dienes 12 and 14 aﬀorded the cycloadducts 13 and 15
stereoselectively in 60% and 94% yields, respectively.
Remarkably, the furan-fused cyclobutenes could undergo the
inverse-electron-demand oxo- and aza -Diels−Alder reaction
with substrates 16 and 17 to furnish polycyclic heterocycles 17
and 19 in good yields. The nitrone 20 could react with furan-
fused cyclobutene species to produce N,O-containing hetero-
cycle 21 in a modest yield when THF was used as solvent. It
should be noted that the reaction mode was di ﬀerent from the
previously reported [4 + 3] cycloaddition,

In conclusion, we reported the generation of furan-fused
cyclobutenes under mild gold catalysis, which could be used as
a platform for [2 + n] cycloadditions. A wide variety of
polycyclic heterocycles bearing cyclobutane at the bridged-
carbons were e ﬃciently constructed in modest to good yields
with good stereoselectivi ty. The selection of other π-
component traps to create structurally complex molecules is
currently under investigation in our laboratory.
